key_insight: A biologically informed dual-branch transformer separates baseline cell state from drug-induced regulatory shifts, enabling accurate prediction of nonlinear dose–time transcriptional responses and robust generalization to unseen cellular contexts.
problem_solved: Predicting how cells' gene expression changes in response to drugs across varying doses and times is confounded by baseline cell-state variation and complex nonlinear dynamics; the paper addresses disentangling these factors to improve accuracy and extrapolation to new cell types or conditions.
method: Dual-branch transformer architecture: one branch models baseline cell state, the other models drug-induced regulatory shifts, and their outputs are combined to predict post-treatment expression.
Biologically informed components: dose–time embeddings and domain knowledge priors (e.g., pathway/regulatory constraints) guide the model to capture realistic perturbation dynamics.
Disentanglement and training objectives that separate inherent cell identity from treatment effects, improving generalization to unseen cellular contexts and nonlinear dose–time behaviors.
impact: Provides a scalable, interpretable framework for perturbation prediction useful in drug discovery, transfer learning and modeling interventions; demonstrates how domain-informed transformers can improve robustness and extrapolation in biological ML tasks.
visual_elements: Schematic of the dual-branch transformer showing baseline branch, perturbation branch, dose–time encoder, and fusion to predicted expression.
Example dose–time trajectories (heatmap or line plots) comparing ground truth vs. model predictions across multiple doses and timepoints.
Latent-space visualization illustrating disentangled baseline vs. drug-shift representations and improved separation for unseen cell types.
Performance bar/line chart comparing generalization accuracy on seen vs. unseen cellular contexts and ablation of biological priors.
paper_title: Modelling drug-induced cellular perturbation responses with a biologically informed dual-branch transformer
paper_authors: Yue Guo, Hao Zhang, Haitao Hu, Jialu Wu, Ji Cao
